_note: An illustrative schedule for the timeline. The model assumes only twelve years of works with even spending (params.build_years); the split of those years between tasks and stages is an assumption made for this page, not a programme. Staging itself is a study point.

network.text: Every train ends in Paris. Changing from one line to another means crossing the city by metro or RER.

Trains from the north, the east and the south-east run through Paris Nord-Est and Gare de Lyon, and some run straight through Paris. Atlantic trains still end at Montparnasse: no through train reaches the Atlantic, and the link is not open.
The four lines are joined in a triangle. Every train stops at two stations, every station has direct trains to all four directions, and TGVs between the Atlantic and the south-east take the link.

seen.name: Gare du Nord and Gare de l’Est

phases.text: Trains run as today. Work sites appear on railway land beside the approach tracks. Some entrances and passages are moved.
Trains run, with fewer platforms at a time. A few platforms are shortened or closed in turn above the works, and some trains leave from other platforms.
The station below is complete; empty trains run through it. New ways down appear in the two halls, still closed. The control hall for London trains is fitted out on the Gare du Nord side.
Trains leave from the deep platforms. The two halls are the entrances. London trains board from a TGV platform closed off for each departure. The surface platforms close and the halls are refitted.
One station with two halls. The surface tracks are closed and cleared; the park on their site can open some years later (assumption).
A terminal on two levels: main-line trains above, RER below.
Trains run as today. Work sites appear beside the tracks towards Bercy.
Trains run, with fewer platforms at a time. A few platforms are closed in turn above the works. The junction cavern for the later link is dug with the station.
Empty trains run through the station below. New ways down appear in the hall, still closed.

Trains leave from the deep platforms and continue to Paris Nord-Est. The surface platforms close and the hall is refitted. The link is joined to the junction cavern from inside, without closing the station.
The hall is the entrance; half the trains continue to Montparnasse by the link. The tracks towards Bercy are closed; the park on their site can open some years later (assumption).
A terminal with platforms one level above the street.
Trains run as today. Work sites appear beside the approach tracks.
Trains run, with fewer platforms at a time. A few platforms are closed in turn above the works. The junction cavern for the link is dug with the station.
All Atlantic trains still end here on the surface, while the other three lines are already joined. Below, the station and the link are being fitted out.
Empty trains run through the station below, towards Paris Nord-Est and over the link to Gare de Lyon. New ways down appear in the hall, still closed.
Trains leave from the deep platforms, half to Paris Nord-Est and half to Gare de Lyon by the link. The surface platforms and the tracks to the ring road close; the park comes later.
